findings.title: Link expiry check is inverted
findings.description: resolve deletes and rejects a link while its expiry is still in the future, but resolves it after expiry. Consequently newly created links immediately return 404 while expired links remain usable until the janitor removes them.

findings.title: First quota increment produces NaN
findings.description: A new owner's quota entry is undefined, so undefined + 1 stores NaN. Every owner therefore gets an invalid quota count on their first link, which serializes as null in the quotas response.

findings.title: Missing Authorization header crashes request handling
findings.description: bearerToken uses a non-null assertion and immediately calls split. An ordinary request without an Authorization header throws a TypeError before handle can return its intended 401 response.

findings.title: Malformed JSON escapes the request error handling
findings.description: JSON.parse executes before the try block, so malformed request bodies throw out of handle instead of producing the endpoint's 400 response.

findings.title: Redirect without a code throws
findings.description: The non-null assertion does not create a runtime value. If the code query parameter is absent, toLowerCase is called on undefined and the request crashes instead of returning a client error or 404.

findings.title: Unnamed reports are written and read under different names
findings.description: exportCsv converts an empty name to links and writes links.csv, but readReport receives the original empty name and tries to read .csv. Thus the default report request writes a file and then returns 500.

findings.title: Reports silently omit links after the first 1000
findings.description: The export always uses store.page(0, 1000), so stores with more than 1000 links produce an incomplete report without any indication of truncation.

findings.title: Empty-store hit average becomes null
findings.description: When the store is empty, totalHits() / size() evaluates to NaN. JSON.stringify converts that to null, so the numeric hits_per_link metric has the wrong value.

findings.title: Cache TTL environment value is multiplied by 1000
findings.description: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is documented as milliseconds, but loadConfig multiplies it by 1000. For example, a requested 300000 ms TTL becomes 300000000 ms.

findings.title: Invalid timeout replaces the default with NaN
findings.description: The invalid-value branch logs that it is keeping the default, but cfg.timeoutMs is assigned NaN unconditionally afterward.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is ignored
findings.description: A positive limit is parsed and then discarded with void limit, leaving cfg.fetchLimit at its previous value. The environment setting therefore has no effect.

findings.title: Configuration validation always succeeds
findings.description: validate returns true even after recording and logging invalid values, so callers cannot distinguish a valid configuration from an invalid one.

findings.title: Startup ignores the validation result
findings.description: The result of validate(cfg) is discarded, so even a corrected validator returning false would not prevent the service from continuing with unusable settings.

findings.title: NaN numeric settings bypass validation
findings.description: Comparisons such as NaN < 1 and NaN > 65535 are both false. Invalid numeric environment values can therefore pass the range checks as if they were valid.

findings.title: Loading configuration mutates the shared defaults
findings.description: cfg references DEFAULT_CONFIG directly. Environment overrides permanently modify the exported default object, and subsequent loadConfig calls can retain values from an earlier environment.

findings.title: Old cache timers can delete refreshed entries
findings.description: Setting an existing code schedules a new timer without cancelling its previous timer. The old timer later calls delete(code) and removes the refreshed value before its new TTL expires. Timer records are also never removed.

findings.title: Eviction is FIFO rather than least-recently-used
findings.description: Eviction always selects the first Map key. get updates entry.used but never changes Map order, and used is never consulted, so frequently accessed old entries are still evicted first.

findings.title: Refreshing an existing entry can evict an unrelated entry
findings.description: When the cache is full, set evicts before checking whether code already exists. Refreshing a non-oldest existing code therefore removes another cached code even though the cache is not gaining an entry.

findings.title: Cache utilization rounds before converting to percent
findings.description: Math.floor(entries.size / limit) is zero for every partially filled cache, so the dashboard reports 0% until the cache is completely full.

findings.title: Cache keys always returns an empty list
findings.description: for...in enumerates object properties rather than Map entries, so it does not visit cached codes. The admin view receives no keys even when the cache is populated.

findings.title: CSV fields are emitted without escaping
findings.description: Targets and owners may contain commas, quotes, or newlines. Writing those values verbatim changes column and row boundaries, producing corrupt reports that cannot be parsed back accurately.

findings.title: Snapshot rename can fail across filesystems
findings.description: The temporary file is always created under /tmp, while the destination directory may be a different mounted filesystem. renameSync then fails with EXDEV and no snapshot is installed.

findings.title: Parsing a generated report adds a spurious blank row
findings.description: Generated reports end with a newline. Splitting that body produces a final empty line, which parseReport converts into a row with an empty first field and undefined remaining fields.

findings.title: Rename validates the source code twice
findings.description: The destination code is never passed to validateCode, so rename can install codes with invalid length or characters.

findings.title: Success rate is rounded to only zero or one hundred
findings.description: Math.floor is applied to the fraction before multiplication. Any partially successful store therefore reports 0%, regardless of the actual proportion.

findings.title: Removing links does not release owner quota
findings.description: delete removes the link but never decrements its owner's count, contrary to the method contract. Expiry and pruning removal paths likewise leave counts behind, so quotas drift upward permanently.

findings.title: Top links are sorted least-popular first
findings.description: The comparator returns a positive value when a has more hits than b, placing higher-hit links later. Slicing the front therefore returns the least-followed links.

findings.title: Owner lookup performs substring matching
findings.description: byOwner promises exact ownership but uses includes. Looking up owner ann also returns links owned by joann or anna, producing an incorrect result set.

findings.title: Extending a link revives expired links
findings.description: extend always replaces expiresAt with a future timestamp. This contradicts the stated final-expiry behavior and makes an already dead code live again.

findings.title: Quota snapshot exposes mutable store state
findings.description: quotas returns the internal object itself. A caller modifying the returned value directly changes the store's accounting, despite the method promising an independent snapshot.

findings.title: Batch import is not atomic
findings.description: Each validated link is inserted immediately. If a later link has an invalid code, earlier links remain stored even though importAll throws, violating the all-or-nothing contract.

findings.title: Prune returns the remaining size instead of removed count
findings.description: The function tracks removed but returns this.links.size. Callers receive an unrelated value whenever the store was nonempty.

findings.title: Target checking rejects instead of reporting a failure
findings.description: probe signals failure by throwing, and Promise.all propagates that rejection. For example, an http target causes checkTargets to reject rather than resolve to that target as its contract promises.

findings.title: Audit flush neither waits nor retries
findings.description: flushAudit invokes write exactly once, discards its promise, and returns immediately. A rejected write becomes unobserved and the audit record is lost despite the retry-until-success contract.

findings.title: Unknown owners have a NaN count
findings.description: For an owner absent from the quota object, quotas[owner] is undefined and adding zero produces NaN instead of the expected count of zero.

findings.title: Stale expiry timers can delete newer cache entries
findings.description: Each set schedules a timeout without cancelling or invalidating the timeout previously associated with that code. If a code is replaced before its original TTL expires, the original callback later calls delete(code) and removes the newer entry prematurely. Evicted and explicitly deleted entries also leave their scheduled work running, while completed handles remain retained in timers.

findings.title: The janitor interval is started without any shutdown path
findings.description: startJanitor returns the only function capable of clearing its interval, but that function is discarded. Once this module is imported, the interval remains live indefinitely; after the surrounding server or host stops, it can keep the Node event loop alive and continue accessing the store.

findings.title: warmCache detaches all probe tasks
findings.description: The async callbacks passed to forEach are not collected or awaited, so warmCache's own promise is fulfilled independently of the probes and cache writes. For example, an insecure target makes the detached callback reject while warmCache reports success, producing an unhandled rejection; with genuinely asynchronous probes, callers can also proceed while the cache is still cold.

findings.title: Audit writes are launched without completion or failure tracking
findings.description: flushAudit discards the promise returned by write and returns void immediately. A caller can report a successful flush, rotate the log, or terminate the process while the write is still pending, and a rejected write becomes an unhandled rejection instead of triggering the documented retry.

findings.title: Client-controlled header grants administrator access
findings.description: The admin endpoint trusts x-admin instead of the authenticated session's role. Any authenticated user can send x-admin: true and retrieve every owner's quota information. The existing requireAdmin helper is also unsuitable as written because its indexOf truthiness check accepts every role except admin.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can delete another user's links
findings.description: deleteLink deletes solely by attacker-supplied code and never compares the link owner with the authenticated session. An ordinary user can obtain codes from the unfiltered listing endpoint and delete every tenant's links.

findings.title: Link listing and reports disclose every tenant's data
findings.description: listLinks returns an unfiltered page containing every link's target, owner, and code to any authenticated user. The report endpoint likewise exports store.page without an ownership filter, allowing cross-tenant enumeration and disclosure.

findings.title: Callers can create records under arbitrary owners
findings.description: createLink takes owner from the request body rather than the verified session. An authenticated attacker can attribute malicious links to another user and corrupt owner-based quota and reporting data.

findings.title: Expired session tokens remain valid indefinitely
findings.description: verify returns a matching session without checking expiresAt. A token stolen before its nominal 12-hour expiry can therefore be replayed until explicit revocation or process restart.

findings.title: Session tokens use a non-cryptographic random generator
findings.description: Bearer tokens are built from Math.random and a predictable timestamp. Math.random is not designed to resist state prediction, so an attacker able to observe issued tokens can potentially predict another user's credential and impersonate that user.

findings.title: Bearer credentials are written to application logs
findings.description: Every newly issued session token is logged in plaintext. Anyone with access to console output, centralized logs, or support diagnostics can replay the token and obtain the owner's privileges.

findings.title: Report name permits directory traversal and arbitrary CSV writes
findings.description: The user-controlled report name is joined directly to the export directory. A name containing ../ components escapes that directory, allowing an authenticated attacker to overwrite any writable path ending in .csv or place a report containing all tenants' data in another accessible directory.

findings.title: Sensitive reports are created with potentially world-readable permissions
findings.description: writeFileSync is called without a restrictive mode despite the report containing every owner's links. Under a common 022 umask the file is created as 0644, allowing other local users to read it.

findings.title: Unescaped CSV fields enable spreadsheet formula injection
findings.description: CSV values are concatenated without quoting or neutralizing formulas. Because an authenticated caller controls owner and target, they can store a value beginning with =, +, -, or @; when support or an administrator opens the exported report in a spreadsheet, the formula can execute and exfiltrate data or launch external content.

findings.title: Click-tracking endpoint is an open redirect
findings.description: The next query parameter is copied directly into Location with no validation or binding to a known link. An authenticated attacker can construct a trusted service URL that redirects recipients to a phishing or malware site.
